SPECIAL KAYE

Loose Women star Kaye Adams makes shock radio return with STV after BBC ‘bully’ sacking

Lynn Kernan , Features Editor
Published: 00:00, 30 Sep 2026
|
Updated: 07:15, 30 Sep 2026
Add us as a preferred source
Comment now

Sponsored by
0:00 / 2:10
Instaread


BROADCASTER Kaye Adams is to return to the airwaves this weekend after being sacked by the BBC amid accusations of bullying.

The Loose Women regular, 63, has landed a one-off gig with STV Radio, co-presenting its Sunday Brunch show with good pal Shereen Nanjiani.

Advertisement

Adams, a long-time member of the STV family, said: “STV has such a special place in my heart and I’m delighted to be back for a trip down memory lane.”

The pair will ease listeners into Sunday with their favourite songs and the stories behind them.

The show marks a return to STV for Nanjiani, 20 years after she left her role as a news anchor.

Meanwhile, Adams joined STV as a news reporter in 1988, covering major stories such as the Lockerbie disaster.

She went on to present its flagship news programme and Scottish Women.

Kaye added: “This show will give her the chance to tell everyone how excruciating my accent was when I walked into STV HQ 38 years ago.”

Shereen said: “I’m delighted to get this chance to co-host with Kaye as STV is where our lifelong friendship began and I have so many happy memories of our time there.

“We’ve had a lot of fun reminiscing and choosing a great playlist of our favourite songs for the show. I’m looking forward to sharing our stories with listeners – even the embarrassing ones.

“It’s been decades since Kaye and I presented a show together so I hope we’re still friends at the end of it.”

David Treasurer, Programme Director at STV Radio, said: “Kaye and Shereen are Scottish broadcasting legends who have both played a huge part in STV’s history, so it feels like a real full circle moment to welcome them as guest hosts of Sunday Brunch on STV Radio.”

The journalist was fired earlier this year from her £155,000-a-year BBC Radio Scotland job.

Advertisement

Allegations include claims she shouted at staff, threw a pen or pencil across a studio and used the C-word.

She denies any wrongdoing and has said she is heartbroken over the “malicious stories”.

She is thought to be considering suing the BBC.
